newsitem.title: UK: Fortnum & Mason sets expansion plan, share issue.
newsitem.headline: Fortnum & Mason sets expansion plan, share issue.

text.p: Fortnum & Mason Plc, the venerable British retailer, on Thursday said it is planning an 11.7 million pound ($18.20 million) expansion to its store in London's Picadilly and will raise 5.1 million pounds via a one-for-eight share rights issue.

The company said it is acquiring leasehold premises adjacent to its Picadilly store, which sells exclusive groceries and also clothes, in a plan that is expected to enlarge its food sale area by about 43 percent and its total sales area by about 23 percent.
Acquisition of the leases, redevelopment and fitting out are expected to total about 11.7 million pounds.
The rights issue will involve issuing up to 1,062,500 shares at five pounds each, following the conversion and sub-division of each ordinary stock unit into 20 new ordinary shares.

Fortnum & Mason said its pretax profits for the financial year ended July 13 rose 11 percent to 3.2 million pounds from 2.9 million last year. Turnover gained six percent to 32.0 million pounds from 30.2 million. The total dividend was increased 10 percent to 158 pence.

"If the proposed major extension to the store is approved there will inevitably be some short term disruption to trading and to operating profits, as well as reduced interest income," the company said in a statement. ($1=.6430 Pound)
